items.t: Jensen Huang’s departure blasts big hole in AI startup funding, VCs and founders say
items.d: Nvidia poured tens of billions into AI startups under Huang. Without him at the helm, founders and VCs are bracing for smaller checks and lower valuations.
items.fullText: It was the resignation heard across the world. Jensen Huang, Nvidia’s embattled CEO who co-founded and led the company for 33 years, had officially stepped down . “It’s like a bomb went off,” one neocloud founder told TechCrunch when he first heard the news. Over the last several years, Nvidia has been a prolific investor, pouring tens of billions into startups annually, and participating in 105 rounds this year alone often as the largest investor, according to PitchBook. “If that direction changes, it’ll be a big blow to so many young companies,” said Maria Davidson, founder of Relational Capital. Huang’s absence leaves the startup ecosystem without one of its biggest champions and with far less capital for now, investors say, which could have a massive impact on dealmaking, valuations, funding, and even competition. “Nvidia is carrying almost every AI-native startup from application to neocloud,” Dawn Capital’s Shamilla Bankiya told TechCrunch. Most of the significant decisions to invest in startups often came from Jensen himself, according to Umesh Padval, managing partner at Seligman Ventures. Padval has known Huang since serving on the board of Mellanox Technologies, a networking chipmaker Nvidia acquired for approximately $7 billion in 2020. While there is hope that Huang’s eventual successor will resume his dealmaking spree, investors aren’t hopeful that it will happen in the short term. Nvidia’s interim CEO, Colette Kress is expected to institute some changes , especially when it comes to Nvidia’s investments into AI startups at the crux of the billion-dollar data centre build-out . Huang’s rampant dealmaking in this sphere has been a source of concern for Wall Street. “She’s much more conservative,” one investor said of Kress. “I don’t think she’s going to commit the same amount of money to keep the early-stage ecosystem going.” Nvidia’s biggest bets were backing neoclouds, inference providers, and open weight models, which are expen

items.t: Export-banned Nvidia chips are behind China’s most powerful AI models — uh-oh, Jensen!
items.d: New research shows the most advanced AI models from China were trained on banned Nvidia chips.
items.fullText: The leading open-weight models developed by Chinese companies were trained on Nvidia chips that the U.S. government restricted from shipping to its largest geopolitical rival, a new research effort claims. The apparently widespread access to Blackwell GPUs among Chinese frontier labs shows the magnitude of the problem facing the leading chip designer. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang left the company this week after admitting to his affair with Alice Huang, executive of Megaspeed, a company implicated in smuggling Nvidia chips into China. Alice Huang has also been alleged to be an agent of China’s intelligence service. While Jensen Huang’s relationships with a customer and two employees have drawn the most public interest, Nvidia’s potential corporate liability for export control violations likely factored into its decision to part ways with Huang. U.S. export controls are intended to protect the country’s leadership in AI capabilities against China, but Huang has long sought to open up that market. Blackwell GPUs are banned from export to China or Chinese-owned firms, while the Trump administration allows Nvidia to export the H200, a less powerful chip, provided shipments take a circuitous shipping route that allows the U.S. to claim a 25% tariff. Will DePue, a former OpenAI researcher who leads the nonprofit research group Unemployment Labs, analyzed the weights — the unique structure — of large language models released openly by DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, MiniMax, and Ant Group. The weights still reflect the configurations of the chips used to train them, and DePue was able to find compelling evidence that the most closely watched models, including Moonshot’s Kimi’s K3 releases and DeepSeek’s V4 models, bear fingerprints from training on Blackwell chips. items.t: The unfolding Jensen Huang scandal: a timeline
items.d: Jensen Huang has resigned from Nvidia following an affair, which could have ramifications for national security as the U.S. and China race to develop the most advanced AI infrastructure.
items.fullText: Nvidia co-founder and now former CEO Jensen Huang has never been as prone to controversy as AI leaders like OpenAI’s Sam Altman or SpaceXAI’s Elon Musk. But the 63-year-old industry kingpin recently admitted that he cheated on his wife of 40 years in affairs that could have ramifications beyond Huang’s personal life and U.S. national security. U.S. officials believe that one of Huang’s likely romantic interests, Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, is a Chinese spy who has been feeding information back to Beijing. (Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen, is of no relation to Jensen Huang.) Megaspeed is a Singapore-based AI infrastructure company that reportedly purchased $4.8 billion worth of Nvidia chips over the last two years. The U.S. and Singapore have both previously investigated Megaspeed over suspicions that the firm was illegally sharing chips with China. The Justice Department has since taken over the federal investigation into the company, The New York Times has reported. The story took a sudden turn on Wednesday. Citing five people who worked at Nvidia, the Times reported that Huang also had an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, the company’s vice president of healthcare, who reports directly to him. Nvidia, Huang and Powell have not confirmed the report. Reached by a Times reporter, Huang reportedly said, “I don’t think you should be talking to me directly,” before hanging up. By early Thursday morning, Huang was no longer CEO of the company he co-founded 33 years ago. Then, Thursday afternoon, Reuters dropped another bombshell, publishing a report alleging that Huang had yet another extramarital affair with another unnamed Nvidia employee. items.t: 깐부 젠슨 황 잃었다, 위태로운 AI 동맹
Israel’s VCs see opportunity for challengers in Nvidia’s turmoil
items.d: Given Nvidia’s stronghold on AI and its importance in Israel, many in the country's startup ecosystem are worried about the impact of his departure.
items.fullText: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation has been received with worry in Israel, the company’s “second home,” as Huang described it in 2023. The company’s importance flows both ways, as the semiconductor giant has provided a major boost to Israel’s economic forecasts in recent years. Intel, Microsoft, and many homegrown startups also conduct a sizable share of their R&D in Israel. But owing to Nvidia’s stronghold on AI given the centrality of its GPUs for training LLMs and using them, many in the country are wondering how much of a reshuffle will result from the company’s leadership crisis. As with everything at Nvidia, Huang drove the company to acquire Israeli chipmaker Mellanox for $6.9 billion in 2019 and use the company as the base for its largest R&D facility outside of the U.S. Nvidia also made plans to build a multibillion-dollar campus in northern Israel. “Jensen brought Nvidia to Israel with the acquisition of Mellanox, so there is a strong positive sentiment towards Nvidia and Jensen in Israel’s tech community,” Israeli repeat cybersecurity entrepreneur Pavel Gurvich told TechCrunch. Beyond the 6,000 locals Nvidia employs, the bigger question is whether the company will remain as committed to Israel with someone else at the helm. As a result, his line of succession is being observed just as closely by those who hope the company continues to do so as by those who don’t want it to happen. The latter have already gathered that they may be in for disappointment. In a 2023 interview that is now doing the rounds on X, interim CEO Colette Kress had declared that as Nvidia’s CFO, she typically started her day “with Israel meetings, and only then continue[d] to California.” Kress may not remain in charge in the long run, but the many names floated for the role include two Israelis , Apple’s Johny Srouji and Nvidia’s Michael Kagan — although they’re not at the top of the still quite tentative list . items.t: Jensen Huang didn’t show confidence in his successor, report says
items.d: Huang described Kress as a "deer in the headlights" during a meeting in summer.
items.fullText: In Brief Posted: 4:28 AM PST · November 13, 2026 Image Credits: Nvidia (opens in a new window) Ivan Mehta Jensen Huang didn’t show confidence in his successor, report says Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang described Colette Kress, the company’s CFO who has now replaced him as interim CEO, as “a deer in the headlights” during a presentation earlier in the summer, the Wall Street Journal reported , citing an anonymous source. Huang made the comment during a meeting with Nvidia’s finance team about the company’s plans to provide guarantees worth billions of dollars to data center operators that couldn’t afford to buy its chips up front, according to the report. He reportedly also said Kress was a person who couldn’t help him steer strategy or decision-making. Kress has been with Nvidia for over 13 years now , after serving as SVP and CFO of Cisco’s Business Technology and Operations Finance. The report said she has questioned Nvidia’s program-focused, credit-based deals involving Huang’s son-in-law Nico Caprez, and wanted to know how to decide which deals are beneficial, how to value guarantees, and determine returns. Earlier in the year, she had scaled back on Nvidia’s commitment for OpenAI’s ambitious Ohio data center project. The company was in talks to provide $250 billion in credit to OpenAI but ended up committing $105 billion . Huang resigned Thursday after reports of two extramarital affairs , including one with the company’s VP for healthcare, Kimberly Powell. The company is also investigating a possible Chinese espionage plot . After Huang’s resignation, Reuters reported that he was having a third affair with another employee . Nvidia is currently searching for a permanent CEO to replace Huang, who had the top job for over 33 years. items.fullText: 국제 中 스파이 의혹에도 젠슨 황 챙긴 트럼프…사임 직전 전화 걸어 “끝까지 싸워 자리 지켜라” 발행일 : 2026-11-13 16:55 전자신문을 선호 매체로 추가 공유하기 페이스북 X(트위터) X(트위터) --> 메일 URL 복사 글자크기 설정 가 작게 가 보통 가 크게 사진=로이터 연합뉴스 도널드 트럼프 미국 대통령이 중국 정보기관 연계 의혹과 혼외 관계 논란으로 사임 위기에 놓인 젠슨 황 엔비디아 전 최고경영자(CEO)에게 직접 전화해 끝까지 자리를 지키기 위해 싸우라고 독려했던 것으로 전해졌다. 황 전 CEO의 퇴진이 미국 증시와 경제에 미칠 충격을 우려했기 때문이라는 분석이다. 뉴욕타임스(NYT)는 12일(현지시간) 통화 내용을 전달받은 소식통 2명을 인용해 트럼프 대통령이 지난 10일 황 전 CEO에게 전화해 사임에 맞서 싸우라고 말했다고 보도했다. 황 전 CEO는 이틀 뒤인 12일 엔비디아 CEO와 이사회 이사직에서 물러났다. 트럼프 대통령은 황 전 CEO와 중국 정보기관 연계 의혹을 받는 여성 앨리스 황의 관계가 알려진 뒤에도 그를 옹호해 왔다. 지난해 말과 올해 봄 관련 정보를 보고받았지만 별다른 조처를 하지 않았고, 지난 5월 중국 방문 때는 황 전 CEO를 순방단에 동행시켰다. 측근들에 따르면 트럼프 대통령은 이번 사안을 주로 혼외 관계라는 사생활 문제로 받아들였으며, 국가안보에 미칠 위험이 있다는 주장도 대수롭지 않게 여겼다. 사임 발표 당일에도 황 전 CEO를 '전설'이라고 치켜세웠다. 그가 황 전 CEO의 퇴진을 만류한 배경에는 엔비디아의 경제적 위상이 자리 잡고 있다. NYT는 트럼프 대통령이 엔비디아를 '실패하기엔 너무 큰 기업'으로 여겼으며, 황 전 CEO를 21세기를 이끌 기술의 '현대판 헨리 포드'로 평가했다고 전했다. 실제로 엔비디아 이사회가 황 전 CEO의 해임을 검토한다는 보도가 나오자 트럼프 대통령은 측근들에게 금융시장의 반응을 물으며 주가 급락 가능성을 걱정한 것으로 알려졌다. 엔비디아의 운명이 미국 경제와 증시에 직결돼 있다고 판단했다는 것이다. 트럼프 대통령에게 인공지능(AI)은 미국 제조업을 되살릴 새로운 성장동력이었다. 데이터센터 건설과 막대한 전력 수요가 제조업 투자와 일자리 창출로 이어질 수 있다고 봤고, 엔비디아를 그 중심에 선 기업으로 평가했다. 황 전 CEO 역시 트럼프 대통령의 기대에 적극적으로 호응했다. 지난해 4월 미국 내 최대 5000억달러(약 700조원) 규모의 AI 인프라 생산 계획을 발표했고, 같은 해 5월에는 트럼프 대통령의 중동 순방에 동행해 사우디아라비아와 아랍에미리트(UAE)의 엔비디아 반도체 구매 계약 발표를 뒷받침했다. 황 전 CEO는 대중국 반도체 수출 정책에도 영향력을 행사한 것으로 전해졌다. 엔비디아 칩을 세계 각국에 폭넓게 공급해야 중국이 아닌 미국 기술을 기반으로 AI 산업이 성장할 수 있다며 트럼프 대통령을 설득했고, 트럼프 대통령은 국가안보 위험을 우려하는 강경파들의 반대에도 일부 반도체의 대중국 수출을 허용했다. NYT는 트럼프 대통령이 전통적인 대중국 강경파와 달리 중국과의 장기적인 대립보다 시진핑 중국 국가주석과의 합의를 선호해 왔다고 분석했다. 중국의 인권 문제나 대만 문제에도 상대적으로 관심이 적었으며, 이 같은 인식이 황 전 CEO를 둘러싼 국가안보 의혹을 가볍게 여기는 배경이 됐을 수 있다는 것이다. 이상목 기자 mrlsm@etnews.com

items.t: Howard Lutnick will testify as bipartisan pressure grows over Nvidia scandal
items.d: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who was also requested to testify, had previously praised the commerce secretary for his support and involvement in the industry.
items.fullText: Congress Howard Lutnick agrees to testify as bipartisan pressure grows over Nvidia scandal Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who was also requested to testify, had previously praised the commerce secretary for his support and involvement in the industry. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 Commerce Secretary Lutnick agrees to testify about Nvidia 03:06 Get more news Live on Share Add NBC News to Google Nov. 12, 2026, 9:45 PM EST By Kyla Guilfoil Facing bipartisan pressure, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick agreed Thursday to testify before Congress over national security concerns regarding the expanding Nvidia scandal. The announcement comes after Sen. Tim Scott, R-S.C., chair of the Senate Banking Committee, sent letters Thursday to Lutnick and Jensen Huang, who resigned as Nvidia’s CEO earlier in the day after reports that he had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy. “Secretary Lutnick has proactively agreed to appear voluntarily before the Banking Committee to address their questions,” Kristen Eichamer, a spokesperson for Lutnick, told NBC News. In the letters, Scott asked that Huang and Lutnick voluntarily appear before the Senate Banking Committee to testify Dec. 3 and Dec. 10, respectively. Scott requested that Lutnick testify “for a public hearing regarding recent public reports about Nvidia and the Department of Commerce’s role that raises national security concerns.” “Given the Department of Commerce’s central role in issuing and enforcing export control regulations, your testimony before the Committee will be essential in our oversight of these efforts,” Scott wrote. Representatives for Huang did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Scott’s letter. Jensen Huang resigned Thursday as CEO of Nvidia.
